correctness.rationale: Stationarity against arbitrary antiderivatives of \(s=x+y\) gives \(\mathbb E[x\mid s]=b\), while antiderivatives of \(y\) give \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid y]=b/y-a\). These imply the support restriction \(0<y\le b/a\), the exact identity \(\operatorname{Var}(x)=\mathbb E[(\dot x+\dot y)^2]=b(\mathbb E[1/y]-1/y_*)\), and the conditional-variance identity \(\operatorname{Var}(x^2)-\operatorname{Var}(b/y-a)=\mathbb E[(\dot y/y)^2]\). In each zero-defect case support invariance forces the unique equilibrium. The packaged checker replayed the critical algebra from its actual staged path.

value.rationale: The Selkov model is a canonical planar model of glycolytic self-oscillation, and modern phase portraits contain genuine stable limit-cycle regimes. The accepted result gives every compact recurrent statistical state two exact fiberwise calibrations rather than only an equilibrium or Hopf calculation. The first converts the elementary mass balance into a sharp harmonic substrate deficit and forces non-equilibrium recurrence to cross the equilibrium production level and undershoot the equilibrium substrate level. The second identifies precisely the unexplained fluctuation of \(x^2\) as mean-square logarithmic substrate speed. These are direct consistency diagnostics for periodic or sampled stationary data and have equality rigidity at the unique equilibrium.
